questions.stem: How does burning fossil fuels contribute to global warming?

options.text: It releases oxygen which traps heat in the atmosphere
It reduces the ozone layer, allowing more UV radiation in
It releases carbon dioxide which acts as a greenhouse gas, trapping heat
It releases nitrogen which makes the atmosphere thicker

questions.explanation: Burning fossil fuels releases carbon dioxide (CO2) into the atmosphere. CO2 is a greenhouse gas that traps infrared radiation (heat) from the Sun, preventing it from escaping back into space. This enhances the greenhouse effect and raises global temperatures.
